page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable, general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1161.28 and multi-core score of 2371.48 fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% of tested servers, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 187.49 GB/sec, which drops to 22.38 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Similarly, database operations and web serving throughput are limited, with static web serving reaching 2.58 GB/sec and Redis SET operations executing at 2.61 million operations per second.

As a burstable instance, the ecs.t6-c1m4.large offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that require occasional bursts of performance. The primary tradeoff is the CPU credit model, which limits sustained high-compute tasks, as reflected in the multi-core Geekbench score of 1822.0 and low software compilation performance. This instance is best suited for light workloads such as low-traffic web servers, small development or testing environments, basic microservices, and simple background task processing.

Running on the KVM hypervisor, it features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU resources, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. Benchmark results place its compute and memory performance in the lower percentiles, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2371.48 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1822.0. Due to its burstable CPU allocation, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent tasks but is limited during sustained execution. It is best suited for light web serving, development environments, and small-scale background processing.
